0.0.n: The お is a customary polite prefix; お菓子 covers sweets and other snacks.

0.1.n: Links the snack category to the product name うまい棒.

0.3.n: Part of the product name うまい棒; うまい is a casual alternative to おいしい.

0.4.n: Completes the product name うまい棒, referring to its stick shape.

0.6.n: Marks うまい棒 as the topic whose price is being discussed.

0.8.n: Combined with 月, 10 names October rather than a quantity of months.

0.9.n: After 10, 月 is read がつ and forms the month name October.

0.10.n: Marks October as the starting point for the higher price.

0.11.n: Names what will rise, followed by the subject marker が.

0.12.n: Identifies 値段 as the thing that goes up.

0.13.n: Polite form of 上がる; the October starting date gives it a future meaning here.

1.0.n: With の, it describes the price as current.

1.1.n: Connects 今 to the following price expression, describing the price at present.

1.2.n: 本 counts long, narrow objects; 1本 is read いっぽん and gives the quantity priced at 12 yen.

1.3.n: States the current price for one stick.

1.4.n: Marks 12 yen as the starting price before the increase.

1.5.n: Directly before 上がって, this amount tells how much the price rises, without needing a particle.

1.6.n: The て-form of 上がる links the increase to its resulting price.

1.8.n: States the new price reached after the increase.

1.9.n: Marks 15 yen as the resulting price with なります.

1.10.n: Polite form of なる; に marks the new state or value.

0.lit: As for the snack Tasty Stick, from October, the price will rise.
0.tip: は introduces the product as the topic, while が marks its price as the thing that rises.

1.lit: From the current one-stick 12 yen, rising 3 yen, it will become 15 yen.
1.tip: から marks the starting price, while に marks the resulting price.
